thread:
emily-ml: FYI nightly smoke on the h100 pool is red across multiple shards — looks like a mix of OOMs and a kernel "invalid device function" from one node. anyone around to triage?
ci-bot: CI failed: nightly/h100-smoke #482
  - failed shards: h100-3, h100-7, h100-5
  - primary errors: OOM during warmup, + kernel log: 'invalid device function'
  - job url: https://ci.internal/redwood/482

sam-infra: can you paste the short logs (dmesg / nvidia-smi) and the image tag used?
emily-ml: image: redwood/inference-nightly:2026-03-16-8a3f
  quick dmesg tail from h100-7:
```
[Mar16 12:02:11] NVRM: GPU 0: PID 23456 (python) UVE: invalid device function
[Mar16 12:02:11] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
[Mar16 12:02:11] kernel: nvidia: module verification failed: signature and/or required key missing
```

emily-ml: nvidia-smi on h100-7 shows driver 535.54, CUDA 12.1 runtime in container

nina-ci: likely driver/runtime mismatch — some hosts still on 535.54, we rolled 535.86 yesterday to part of fleet. can we confirm host driver on all 3 nodes?
mat: also possible kernel module ABI mismatch after kernel update (we had a kernel rollout last night). if module built against old kernel, "invalid device function" can show up.

emily-ml: here's the command i used to fetch logs:
```
kubectl exec -it pod/nightly-smoke-482 -- bash -c "nvidia-smi -q; dmesg | tail -n 50" > /tmp/ci-h1007.log
```

sam-infra: quick triage plan:
  1) confirm host driver version on h100-3/5/7 (run `modinfo nvidia` and `cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version`)
  2) if driver versions differ, rerun shard with pinned driver or move pod to a node with 535.86
  3) if drivers match, collect core dump and nv-hostengine logs and open a bisect request

emily-ml: i kicked a rerun pinned to nodes with the newer driver (tagged 'driver-pinned-53586') — i'll paste results in a few mins

(ci-bot): rerun started: nightly/h100-smoke #482-retry-1 (pinned driver nodes)

emily-ml: rerun finished:
  - h100-3: PASS
  - h100-5: PASS
  - h100-7: FAIL (OOM during model warmup)

emily-ml: h100-7 OOM snippet:
```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 48.00 GiB (GPU 0; 80.00 GiB total; 60.12 GiB already allocated; 1.25 GiB free; 58.88 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
  at /root/.cache/pip/wheels/.../torch/alloc.cpp:312
```

mat: that OOM looks like real memory pressure not a kernel abort. could be multi-tenant interference on h100-7; can we check nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps for that host?

nina-ci: also, the earlier "invalid device function" entry suggests at least one process hit a bad kernel. we need the full nvidia-bug-report + kernel logs from h100-7. emily, can you collect:
```
sudo nvidia-bug-report.sh --logfile /tmp/bugreport-h1007.tar.gz
sudo cp /var/log/kern.log /tmp/kern-h1007.log
```

emily-ml: on it. uploading bugreport to the ci job artifacts. link: https://ci.internal/artifacts/482/bugreport-h1007.tar.gz

sam-infra: i'm happy to run a narrow bisect — next step: if the bugreport shows module build mismatches, we bisect kernel rollouts; otherwise bisect the container layers (we have image history for the nightly tag). who should I assign?
emily-ml: assign to @sam-infra, please. i've added notes in the issue: https://issue.internal/REDWOOD-1234

sam-infra: taking it. I'll start with host-side driver/kernel checks and then do a container layer bisect if needed.

ci-bot: Created task REDWOOD-1234 and added label 'triage/h100'

emily-ml: thanks all. tagging @mat to watch for multi-tenant noisy neighbors on h100-7 tomorrow during warmup window. :thumbsup:

mat: ack, i'll run a noise check on h100-7 overnight and add metric dashboards for memory churn.

emily-ml: closing the slack thread — follow-up will be in REDWOOD-1234 with bisect results. cheers! :rocket:
